questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(19, 456, 6)

questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 

(19, 456, 6)

__19 × 6____** × 4**__ = 456

456 = 456 (LHS = RHS)

And,

(16, 320, 5)

320 = 320 (LHS = RHS)

504 ≠ 378 (LHS ≠ RHS)

__14 × 5____ × 4__ = 210

280 ≠ 210 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3) (21, 504, 8)

__21 × 8____ × 4__ = 504

672 ≠ 504 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4) (18, 648, 9)

__18 × 9____ × 4__ = 648

**648 = 648 (LHS = **RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '(18, 648, 9)' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(9, 82)
questions.solution:

(12, 145)

__12²__ + 1 = 145

__**144 + 1**__ = 145

145 = 145 (LHS = RHS)

And,

(9, 82)

__81 + 1__ = 82

82 = 82 (LHS = RHS)

So, checking each option one by one:

Option 1) (16, 256)

__162__ + 1 = 256

__256 + 1__ = 256

257 ≠ 256 (LHS ≠ RHS)

__196 + 1__ = 197

**197 = 197 (LHS = RHS)**

Option 3) (22, 483)

__222__ + 1 = 483

__484 + 1__ = 483

485 ≠ 483 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4) (8, 69)

__82__ + 1 = 69

__64 + 1__ = 69

65 ≠ 69 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '(14, 197)' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits.

E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Option 1) 36 – 84

36 × 7 ÷ 3 = 84

__**252 ÷ 3**__ = 84

84 = 84 (LHS = RHS)

Option 2) 72 – 168

72 × 7 ÷ 3 = 168

__504 ÷ 3__ = 168

168 = 168 (LHS = RHS)

Option 3) 66 – 154

66 × 7 ÷ 3 = 154

__462 ÷ 3__ = 154

154 = 154 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4) 33 – 72

33 × 7 ÷ 3 = 72

__231 ÷ 3__ = 72

**77 ≠ 72 (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Thus, out of all the options, '33 – 72' is the odd one out.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(34, 47, 62)

(119, 142, 167)

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

(34, 47, 62)

34 + 2 = 36 ⇒ Perfect square of 6

47 + 2 = 49 ⇒ Perfect square of 7

62 + 2 = 64 ⇒ Perfect square of 8

And,

(119, 142, 167)

119 + 2 = 121 ⇒ Perfect square of 11

142 + 2 = 144 ⇒ Perfect square of 12

167 + 2 = 169 ⇒ Perfect square of 13

So, checking each option one by one:

Option 1) (27, 38, 51)

27 + 2 = 29 ⇒ Not a perfect square

38 + 2 = 40 ⇒ Not a perfect square

51 + 2 = 53 ⇒ Not a perfect square

Option 2) (48, 65, 82)

48 + 2 = 50 ⇒ Not a perfect square

65 + 2 = 67 ⇒ Not a perfect square

82 + 2 = 84 ⇒ Not a perfect square

Option 3) (64, 78, 99)

64 + 2 = 66 ⇒ Not a perfect square

78 + 2 = 80 ⇒ Not a perfect square

99 + 2 = 111 ⇒ Not a perfect square

Option 4) (79, 98, 119)

79 + 2 = 81 ⇒ Perfect square of 9

98 + 2 = 100 ⇒ Perfect square of 10

119 + 2 = 121 ⇒ Perfect square of 11

Thus, out of all the options, '(79, 98, 119)' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means ‘A is the son of B’,

A − B means ‘A is the sister of B’,

A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and

A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’.

Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P ÷ Q × R − M + T’?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aecbe9ab6b7da7cca1ac2d356e84b8c992ce57c8b50affd73dfdd3dad30ceb2e.png] 

Decoding symbols:

 
 

 
 A is
 
 

 Symbol
 +
 −
 ×
 ÷
 
 

 Meaning
 Son
 Sister
 Brother
 Mother
 
 

 
 to B
 
 

Given: P ÷ Q × R − M + T

P ÷ Q → P is the mother of Q.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d36b92d0118173160385825f8149c357487d7c6fea7ef30c316c50d0d948c1b.png] 

Q × R → Q is the brother of R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42b8c95aa65a1c1f182cbc7e23e8d4126d9a1a166d08a12db8792f4469e80a66.png] 

R − M → R is the sister of M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/80494ef529a7a29b15d7e6c060ee85f282822e07af84c9c69ad0bc07dc881b1c.png] 

M + T → M is the son of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22b5ad680d8c2120767c479e43835a3f9e917500a8f16f4320f4caefa2953909.png] 

Thus, T is P's husband.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4"
